blogPosts.title: How Much Does a Home Extension Cost in Glen Waverley in 2026?
blogPosts.excerpt: Thinking of adding space to your Glen Waverley home? We break down the real costs, from single-storey rear extensions to second-storey additions, with 2026 pricing.
body: If you're a homeowner in Glen Waverley or one of the surrounding eastern suburbs, you've probably wondered about the cost of extending your home. Whether it's a new open-plan living area, an extra bedroom, or a second storey, the price tag depends on several local factors. In 2026, material costs have stabilised but labour is still in high demand across Melbourne's east. A single-storey rear extension typically starts around $80,000 for a basic 20sqm room, but can climb to $200,000+ for a full-width living space with kitchen and bathroom. The exact figure depends on your site conditions, the complexity of the design, and whether you need to work with sloping blocks — common in parts of Glen Waverley.

One of the biggest cost drivers is the foundation type. Melbourne's clay soils, especially in areas like Mount Waverley and Wheelers Hill, require deeper footings and sometimes screw piles to manage movement. This can add $10,000–$20,000 to your project before you even start building. That's why a proper site inspection is critical. At Skilled Builders, we always walk the block before giving a ballpark — and we factor in soil tests and engineering reports upfront. No surprises later.

After foundations, the structural framing and roof make up about 30% of your extension budget. If you're adding a second storey, you'll need to reinforce the existing ground-floor walls, which adds significant cost but also gives you the most value in terms of added square metres. A double-storey extension in Glen Waverley can range from $150,000 to $400,000 depending on size and finishes. We've found that many families prefer to stay in their home during the build, so we phase the work to minimise disruption — keeping the kitchen and bathroom operational as long as possible.

Interior fit-out costs vary wildly. Basic carpet and paint might cost $15,000–$25,000, while premium joinery, stone benchtops, and European appliances can push it to $60,000+. We always present three finish levels: standard, premium, and luxury — so you can choose what fits your budget. And because we're a local Glen Waverley builder, we know which suppliers in the area offer the best value. For example, we source timber from local yards and use Melbourne-based cabinet makers to keep transport costs down.

Don't forget the 'hidden' costs: council permits, survey fees, and engineering certifications add another $8,000–$15,000 to most projects. In Monash City Council (which covers Glen Waverley), a planning permit is required for most extensions that change the building envelope. We handle the entire approval process as part of our service, so you don't have to deal with red tape. Our close relationship with council planners means faster turnaround — often 4–6 weeks instead of the typical 8–12.

Finally, a word on return on investment. A well-designed extension in Glen Waverley can add 15–25% to your property value, especially if it creates open-plan living or adds a second storey. The suburb's median house price continues to climb, and families are willing to pay a premium for move-in-ready homes with extra space. If you're planning to sell within 5 years, an extension is typically a better investment than a full renovation. Get in touch for a free on-site consultation — we'll give you a realistic cost range and help you decide what's best for your home.

blogPosts.title: Knockdown Rebuild vs Renovation: Which is Best for Your Melbourne Home?
blogPosts.excerpt: Deciding between demolishing and rebuilding or renovating your existing home? We compare costs, timelines, and outcomes for homeowners in Melbourne's eastern suburbs.
body: Every week we talk to families in Glen Waverley, Box Hill, and Camberwell who are torn between knocking down their old home and rebuilding, or investing in a major renovation. Both paths have their pros and cons, and the right choice depends on the condition of your existing home, your budget, and your long-term plans. In 2026, with land values high in Melbourne's east, a knockdown-rebuild often makes financial sense if your current house is structurally unsound or has outdated floor plans.

Let's start with knockdown rebuild. The biggest advantage is that you get a brand new home tailored to modern living — open-plan layouts, energy-efficient insulation, double glazing, and smart wiring. The total cost ranges from $300,000 for a basic 3-bedroom home to $600,000+ for a luxury 4-bedroom design. The process takes 12–18 months from initial consultation to handover. You'll also need to factor in demolition costs ($15,000–$25,000) and living expenses if you rent during the build. But you end up with a zero-maintenance home that meets all current building codes.

Renovation, on the other hand, can be cheaper and faster if the structure is sound. A full home renovation in a suburb like Mount Waverley typically costs $150,000–$350,000 and takes 6–12 months. You can stay in the house for part of the build (though it's disruptive), and you avoid the cost of demolition and new foundations. However, you're limited by the existing layout — you can't easily add a second storey without major structural work, and you may have to deal with old wiring, plumbing, and asbestos. Older homes in Box Hill often have asbestos in the ceilings or floor tiles, adding $5,000–$10,000 for safe removal.

One key factor that many homeowners overlook is the site's zoning and building envelope. In established suburbs like Camberwell and Canterbury, heritage overlays and strict council regulations can severely limit what you can do with a renovation. A knockdown rebuild gives you a clean slate, but you still need to comply with setback rules and height limits. Skilled Builders works closely with councils across Melbourne's east to navigate these rules — we'll tell you upfront if your dream renovation is actually feasible under current planning laws.

Timeline is another differentiator. If you need to move in quickly (e.g., you've sold your current home), a renovation can be faster than a full rebuild. But if you have the flexibility, a knockdown rebuild often saves you from doing 'band-aid' fixes that never quite feel right. We've seen many families who renovated first, then regretted not knocking down — they ended up spending twice the money to get the home they really wanted.

Our advice? Start with a free on-site consultation. We'll assess your existing home's structure, check the council overlays, and give you a honest recommendation. Whether you choose a knockdown rebuild or a major renovation, Skilled Builders has the experience to deliver a beautiful, functional home on budget. Call us today to book a walk-through of your Glen Waverley, Mount Waverley, or Box Hill property.

blogPosts.title: The Complete Guide to Home Extensions in Melbourne's Unpredictable Weather
blogPosts.excerpt: Extending your home in Melbourne's east? Learn how to design for hot summers, cold winters, and everything in between — from insulation to drainage.
body: Melbourne's weather is famous for being 'four seasons in one day', and that's especially true in the eastern suburbs like Glen Waverley, Doncaster, and Templestowe. If you're planning a home extension, you need to design for extremes: scorching summer days above 40°C, sudden thunderstorms, and chilly winter mornings. A well-designed extension should keep your family comfortable year-round without running up huge energy bills.

Start with orientation. In Melbourne's southern hemisphere position, north-facing extensions are ideal for passive solar heating. Large north-facing windows allow winter sun to warm the living areas, while adequate eaves block summer heat. We always recommend a north-south layout for rear extensions — it captures natural light and reduces reliance on artificial heating and cooling. In Wheelers Hill and Mount Waverley, many blocks are slightly sloping, so we also factor in cross-ventilation by placing windows on opposite walls.

Insulation is non-negotiable for Melbourne's climate. We use R5.0 ceiling insulation and R2.5 wall batts as standard — anything less will cost you in energy bills. Double-glazed windows with low-E coating are a must for any new extension; they keep heat inside during winter and reflect solar radiation in summer. The upfront cost is around $1,000–$1,500 per window, but it pays for itself within 5–7 years. Skilled Builders also installs vapour barriers and breathable membranes to prevent moisture buildup — a common problem in Melbourne's humid summers.

Drainage is another critical factor. Melbourne's east gets heavy rainfall in spring and autumn, and clay soils in areas like Burwood and Clayton can become waterlogged. Your extension's roof must have adequate guttering and downpipes, and we always install a French drain or slot drain around the perimeter to direct water away from the foundations. We've seen too many extensions with damp issues because the builder skimped on drainage. Our team ensures all surfaces slope away from the house and that stormwater is connected to the council's network.

Heating and cooling should also be planned early. Split-system air conditioners are the most common choice, but for a seamless look, we often integrate ducted reverse-cycle systems into the extension. Underfloor heating is popular for bathrooms and open-plan areas — it's comfortable and efficient, especially when paired with carpet or timber floors. We recommend zoning the system so you only heat or cool the rooms you're using. Smart thermostats and energy-recovery ventilators (ERVs) are becoming standard in 2026 for maximising comfort and efficiency.

Finally, think about outdoor living. A well-designed deck or pergola extends your usable space and supports the indoor-outdoor flow that Melbourne families love. We use hardwood decking like Spotted Gum or Modwood (composite) that withstands UV and moisture without warping. For pergolas, adjustable louvered roofs let you control sun and shade. When done right, your extension will be a pleasure to live in through every season. Let Skilled Builders design your weather-smart extension — call us for a free quote today.

blogPosts.title: Second-Storey Additions in Melbourne's East: Costs, Permits & Design Tips
blogPosts.excerpt: Considering adding a second storey to your home? Learn about costs, council permits, and design considerations for double-storey extensions in Melbourne's east.
body: As families grow and land prices in Melbourne's east keep rising, more homeowners are looking up instead of out. A second-storey addition is a smart way to add significant living space — often an extra 60–100 square metres — without sacrificing your backyard. In suburbs like Glen Waverley, Mount Waverley, and Box Hill, where blocks are typically between 500 and 700 square metres, a double-storey extension can transform a dated three-bedder into a spacious four-bedroom family home.

The cost of a second-storey addition in Melbourne's east typically ranges from $200,000 to $400,000 as of early 2026. The price depends on the size, the complexity of the design, and the condition of your existing ground-floor structure. Most homes built before 2000 have single-brick walls that aren't designed to support a second storey. That means we need to install steel columns or reinforced concrete beams to transfer the load — an added expense of $20,000–$50,000. However, if your home already has a solid concrete slab and cavity brick walls, the upgrade is cheaper.

Council permits are a major consideration. In Monash City Council (Glen Waverley, Mount Waverley) and Whitehorse Council (Box Hill, Burwood), a planning permit is required for any second-storey addition that exceeds certain height limits or is visible from the street. We've found that many homeowners are surprised by the strict 'neighbourhood character' rules — you can't just build a box on top. The design must respect the existing streetscape, with setbacks and roof forms that blend in. Skilled Builders has an in-house designer who works with council planners to get permits approved quickly — often within 8 weeks.

Structural engineering is critical for second-storey work. We engage a structural engineer to assess your existing footings, walls, and roof trusses. In many cases, the ground floor needs additional steel bracing or underpinning. If your home is on clay soil — common in Wheelers Hill and Notting Hill — we may recommend screw piles to prevent differential settlement. These engineering reports cost $2,000–$5,000 but are essential for a safe and stable build. Skipping them can lead to cracking and movement down the track.

Living through a second-storey addition is manageable but requires planning. We usually keep the ground floor operational for the first 6–8 weeks while we complete the structural work above. We set up temporary weatherproofing and maintain access to kitchen and bathroom. Once the upper floor is framed and roofed, we switch focus to internal finishes on both levels. The total build time is 6–10 months. We provide weekly progress photos and site meetings so you're always in the loop.

The payoff? A second-storey addition can increase your property value by 20–30% in Melbourne's east, especially if you add bedrooms and a rumpus room that maximise the home's functionality. And you keep your prime location — no need to move to another suburb and pay stamp duty again. If you're curious about whether your home can support a second storey, call Skilled Builders for a free on-site assessment. We'll give you an honest answer and a fixed-price quote.
